Short answer
- No — the sender does not see anything different if you archive vs delete a message. Those actions affect only your copy of the message in your mailbox, not the sender’s copy or their mailbox.

What generally happens (recipient-side)
- Archive: removes the message from your Inbox view and places it in an Archive/All Mail folder or gives it an “archive” label. The message remains in your mailbox, searchable and retrievable, and is not in Trash.
- Delete: moves the message to your Trash/Deleted Items (or immediately permanently deletes, depending on settings). Messages in Trash are usually recoverable until you empty the Trash or until the provider’s retention period ends; after that they may be permanently removed.
- Sync behavior: with IMAP (typical for modern email), archive/delete actions sync across devices. With POP, behavior depends on client settings (messages may be removed from server or left there).
- Backups and server retention: even after you delete a message it may still exist in provider backups or logs for some time.

Consequences & risks
- Sender is unaffected and receives no notification.
- Deleting is more likely to lead to permanent loss (after Trash retention ends). Archiving is safer if you may need the message later.
- If you need to free storage, deleting (and then emptying Trash) reduces your storage quota; archiving usually does not free storage (it stays in your mailbox).

If you want provider-specific details or official citations, tell me which email service and confirm you want me to look them up. If you want me to perform a destructive action (delete/empty trash) in an account, I will first need the exact target and your explicit confirmation.
